title: One-Pot Creamy Broccoli & White Bean Rice
description: Rice, broccoli, and white beans cook into a simple creamy one-pot dinner with ordinary pantry and freezer ingredients.
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use Monterey Jack or mozzarella instead of cheddar.

cookSteps.text: Combine 1 cup rice, 2 cups broth, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, and reduce to low.
Cook for 12 minutes, then quickly stir in 2 cups chopped broccoli and 1 can white beans. Cover again and cook 6–8 minutes, until the rice and broccoli are tender.
Stir in 1/2 cup milk and 3/4 cup shredded cheddar over low heat until creamy and the cheese is melted, about 2 minutes.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat with a splash of milk or broth.

title: Turkey, Cabbage & Apple Crunch Wraps
description: Deli turkey, crisp cabbage, and apple make a fresh fast wrap with a simple creamy mustard dressing.
substitutions: Use deli ham instead of turkey.
Use plain yogurt instead of mayonnaise.
Use shredded carrots instead of some of the cabbage.

cookSteps.text: Stir 2 tablespoons mayonnaise and 1 teaspoon mustard in a small bowl. Toss with 1 1/2 cups sliced cabbage.
Lay out 2 tortillas. Divide 4 ounces deli turkey, the dressed cabbage, and 1/2 sliced apple between them.
Fold in the sides, roll tightly, and serve immediately.

storage: Best assembled fresh. Refrigerate the filling separately up to 2 days.

title: Leftover Mashed Potato & Egg Breakfast Cakes
description: Leftover mashed potatoes become crisp little breakfast cakes with egg and cheese instead of another reheated side dish.
substitutions: Use mozzarella or Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.
Stir in 2 tablespoons chopped deli ham if desired.

steps.text: Mix and shape the potato cakes.

cookSteps.text: Mix 1 1/2 cups cold mashed potatoes, 1 egg, 1/2 cup shredded cheddar, 2 tablespoons flour, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Shape into 4 patties.
Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Cook the patties for 4–5 minutes per side, until browned and hot through.

storage: Refrigerate cooked cakes up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet or toaster oven for the best texture.

title: Small-Batch Cinnamon Applesauce Cake
description: A small soft cinnamon snack cake uses applesauce for moisture and needs only everyday baking staples.
substitutions: Use white sugar instead of brown sugar.
Use neutral oil instead of melted butter.
Skip the vanilla if you do not have it.

steps.text: Bake until the center is set.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a small baking dish. Stir together 3/4 cup flour, 1/3 cup brown sugar, 1/2 teaspoon baking soda, and 1 teaspoon cinnamon.
Stir in 1/2 cup applesauce, 1 egg, 2 tablespoons melted butter or oil, and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla if using, just until no dry flour remains.
Spread in the dish and bake for 22–25 minutes, until the center springs back lightly and a toothpick comes out without wet batter.

storage: Keep covered at room temperature up to 2 days or refrigerate up to 5 days.
